privacy_assertions: No selected-tab mutation is required to open the search surface.
A superseded query response is not rendered.
Fixture output excludes raw query text and URL values.
Event diagnostics contain only bounded reason codes and counts.
No stale result is served before authoritative snapshot recovery.
Rejected result references do not select a replacement tab silently.
Status contains no raw tab metadata.
Reset affects only InfoBoard-owned records and paths.
Denied or excluded browser data is not requested, collected, persisted, or transmitted.

future_check_contracts.scope: Formatting and static lint by language
future_check_contracts.selection_rule: Select formatter and linter only after each implementation module and its language toolchain are observed; do not choose a project command now.
future_check_contracts.pass_signal: All changed source and fixture files pass the selected deterministic formatter/linter with no diagnostics.

future_check_contracts.selection_rule: Use the test runner established by the owning language/module scaffold; exercise phase fixtures and observable contracts.
future_check_contracts.pass_signal: Every targeted behavior and boundary assertion passes with no external service or live user data.

future_check_contracts.selection_rule: Choose integration harness after extension/host interfaces and their fixture adapters exist; use local deterministic inputs.
future_check_contracts.pass_signal: Handshake, snapshot, query, activation, recovery, and persistence seams report their declared states and no partial/stale result.

future_check_contracts.selection_rule: Select browser binaries and runner after IP-03 establishes the adapter and supported browser harness.
future_check_contracts.pass_signal: The same fixtures pass in Chrome and Edge with focused input, expected results, safe activation, and unchanged browser state on dismissal.

future_check_contracts.selection_rule: Choose automated audit and screen-reader procedures after IP-13 provides a rendered surface and browser harness.
future_check_contracts.pass_signal: Keyboard, visible focus, semantics, contrast, reduced motion, scaling, and narrow-window acceptance all pass.

future_check_contracts.selection_rule: Choose benchmark runner only after IP-01/phase owners declare the implementation runtime and reference hardware; retain the stated NFR budgets.
future_check_contracts.pass_signal: Measured p95 values meet the owned NFR thresholds and reports include sample counts, environment, and allocation or memory evidence.

future_check_contracts.selection_rule: Use the package entry points and disposable profiles defined by IP-18; do not invent an installer or platform command before then.
future_check_contracts.pass_signal: Install/upgrade/repair/uninstall reach their expected health and ownership postconditions without unrelated browser-data mutation.

future_check_contracts.scope: Planning corpus traceability and fixture validation
future_check_contracts.selection_rule: Run `python3 tests/implementation/validate_corpus.py` from repository root. The stdlib-only validator is established by IP-01; extend it only when the catalog or phase contract changes.
future_check_contracts.pass_signal: Exit zero only when requirement ownership, task/commit mappings, fixture schema shape, stable IDs, local links, and all phase acceptance seams validate; a malformed corpus exits nonzero.

global_invariants.statement: Only the current browser profile and its authorized context may contribute to a projection, query, result reference, or durable record.
global_invariants.observable_guard: A cross-profile input is rejected before mutation and produces no cross-profile result or activation reference.

global_invariants.statement: Projection revisions advance only for accepted effective changes within their current epoch; stale or conflicting work cannot publish partial state.
global_invariants.observable_guard: Accepted revisions are monotonic, rejected events leave the last committed projection unchanged, and stale epochs require an authoritative snapshot.

global_invariants.statement: Identical projection, query, timestamp, context, and ranking-model inputs produce identical ordered results and explanations.
global_invariants.observable_guard: Repeated fixture runs produce byte-equivalent ordered opaque IDs, scores, and bounded explanation data despite candidate insertion-order changes.

global_invariants.statement: Diagnostics and status output exclude raw titles, full URLs, query strings, page contents, credentials, and private record values.
global_invariants.observable_guard: Synthetic sensitive sentinels are absent from every emitted diagnostic/status record; only bounded counts, versions, states, and error classes remain.

global_invariants.statement: Payloads, record counts, request durations, and concurrency are bounded before allocation or partial application.
global_invariants.observable_guard: At-bound inputs pass; over-bound inputs return a typed bounded failure with no partial state mutation or unbounded queued work.

global_invariants.statement: Browser activation fails closed unless the selected result's profile, identity, epoch, revision, and current browser state are explicitly valid.
global_invariants.observable_guard: Stale, removed, reused, or mismatched references produce zero activation calls and never silently select another tab.

global_invariants.statement: Reset and uninstall remove only InfoBoard-owned local state and never mutate browser tabs, history, or unrelated user data.
global_invariants.observable_guard: Owned records are absent after cleanup while unrelated sentinels and browser state remain unchanged; repeating cleanup is idempotent.

phase_seams.handoff_note: Shared convergence baseline only; IP-02's profile/identity fixtures remain mandatory.

phase_seams.acceptance_signal: The extension-owned search surface opens and input is focused before text entry.
phase_seams.handoff_note: IP-03 owns this shared command/focus fixture.

phase_seams.acceptance_signal: Normalized browser events converge to the eligible full-snapshot oracle without duplicate identities.
phase_seams.handoff_note: IP-04 owns this shared browser-event fixture.

phase_seams.acceptance_signal: Projection handoff exposes the exact committed eligible identity set.
phase_seams.handoff_note: Baseline only; IP-05 revision, atomicity, and recovery fixtures extend this seam.

phase_seams.acceptance_signal: Unavailable host is visible and retryable without claiming query results.
phase_seams.handoff_note: Baseline failure signal; IP-06 owns process lifecycle and fresh-session acceptance.

phase_seams.acceptance_signal: Reconnect requests an authoritative snapshot before declaring ready.
phase_seams.handoff_note: Baseline only; protocol framing, limits, and typed errors remain IP-07-owned.

phase_seams.acceptance_signal: Reset removes owned records and leaves external/browser sentinels unchanged.
phase_seams.handoff_note: Baseline only; IP-08 migration, corruption, and retention fixtures extend storage coverage.

phase_seams.acceptance_signal: Ready is published only after authoritative snapshot and index revisions match.
phase_seams.handoff_note: IP-09 owns reconnect convergence for this shared fixture.

phase_seams.acceptance_signal: Only the latest accepted query revision is reflected in the live result state.
phase_seams.handoff_note: Shared query handoff only; IP-10 owns normalizer/index-specific fixtures.

phase_seams.acceptance_signal: Repeated identical ranking inputs produce the same ordered identities and scores.
phase_seams.handoff_note: IP-11 owns deterministic ranking behavior and extends this fixture.

phase_seams.acceptance_signal: Rendered results correspond to the latest accepted query revision.
phase_seams.handoff_note: IP-12 owns the query API and live-query fixture.

phase_seams.acceptance_signal: Keyboard journey begins with the query input focused before text is accepted.
phase_seams.handoff_note: Shared baseline only; IP-13 owns UI keyboard, semantic, and accessibility extensions.

phase_seams.acceptance_signal: Stale result produces zero browser activation calls and no silent replacement.
Reset removes InfoBoard-owned records while preserving unrelated data and open tabs.
phase_seams.handoff_note: IP-15 owns reset/uninstall lifecycle; broader cleanup scenarios remain phase-specific.

phase_seams.acceptance_signal: Host failure is surfaced as bounded, actionable, retryable status.
phase_seams.handoff_note: IP-16 owns health and diagnostics; its full transition suite extends this baseline.

phase_seams.acceptance_signal: Denied capability fails closed; excluded browser data is not accepted or emitted.
phase_seams.handoff_note: IP-17 owns privacy/permission policy; its abuse matrix extends this baseline.

phase_seams.acceptance_signal: The packaged compatible pair preserves the shared live-query result contract.
phase_seams.handoff_note: Baseline only; IP-18's artifact and installer lifecycle fixtures are required for packaging acceptance.

phase_seams.acceptance_signal: The same accepted query result is observed in each declared compatibility cell.
phase_seams.handoff_note: Baseline only; six-cell hardware, performance, privacy, and accessibility evidence remains required.

phase_seams.acceptance_signal: Release evidence refers to a result contract reproduced by the candidate artifacts.
phase_seams.handoff_note: Aggregation baseline only; IP-20 release gates and rollback evidence remain mandatory.
